The Transformer did not emerge without predecessors. Its history combines attention mechanisms developed for neural machine translation, self-attention, large-scale training, and different objectives across model families. This selective timeline highlights milestones; it is neither exhaustive nor a claim of a single causal path.

## Placing LLMs in the AI landscape

This classification helps distinguish **the kind of method** an LLM belongs to from **the problem domain** in which it is used. It complements the timeline; it is not a step in a model's computation.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  subgraph AI["Artificial intelligence"]
    subgraph ML["Machine learning"]
      subgraph DL["Deep learning<br/>(neural networks)"]
        LLM["LLM"]
      end
    end
  end
  NLP["NLP: a domain of problems<br/>(rules, statistics, models, LLMs…)"]
```

- **Deep learning** denotes a family of methods: neural networks with multiple layers. Current LLMs belong to it.
- **Natural language processing** (NLP) denotes a domain of problems: processing or producing language. It is addressed by very different methods — linguistic rules, statistical models, specialized systems, and neural networks. LLMs are a dominant but not exclusive answer: a production system can combine rules, specialized models, document retrieval, tools, and LLMs.
- The term **LLM** has no universal numerical threshold: it generally refers to language models trained at large scale, using substantial data and compute. The *foundation model* concept instead emphasizes reuse: a model serving as a base for many applications. The concepts are related, but they are not synonyms.

## Timeline

To reconnect this timeline with the conceptual course, return to the [LLM panorama](llm-overview.qmd); to compare the architecture families discussed across milestones, see the dedicated [Transformer architectures page](transformer-architectures.qmd).

Dates distinguish submissions, announcements, and releases. Milestones are grouped by research area; chronological order does not imply a single causal chain.

{{< include /includes/_history-timeline-en.qmd >}}


## What the timeline should not imply

- **Transformer does not mean autoregressive LLM.** The 2017 paper presents an encoder-decoder architecture for translation; BERT uses an encoder and a masked prediction objective.
- **Attention predates the Transformer.** The 2017 paper assembles and reorganizes existing ideas into a coherent architecture; it did not invent the entire family of attention mechanisms.
- **Scale does not explain everything.** Data, objectives, tokenization, architecture, training procedure, and evaluation also shape observed capabilities.
- **A publication date is not proof of absolute priority.** This page selects a few pedagogical milestones and does not attempt to catalogue every parallel contribution.
